patch_description: Add a final coordinate-descent "pair-exchange" perturbation phase after the fine polish, following the recommendation. All top programs plateau at ~0.03 (vs. the ~0.037-0.040 optimum), suggesting trapped local minima where the binding vertex of the smallest triangle cannot improve by continuous moves. The structured move: identify the vertices of the smallest triangles ("binding" points) and swap one with a "free" point whose incident triangle areas are all comfortably large, then re-run a short hard-min polish (decaying steps 0.01→1e-4, ~3k iters) from the swapped configuration. Keep the result only if the true best improves. Per-vertex binding scores are computed cheaply with the existing vectorized `_all_areas` machinery via `np.minimum.reduceat`-style accumulation over the (165,3) triplet index array. This restarts the local search in a new basin without sacrificing the incumbent. Runtime increases modestly (~2000 swap attempts × short polish would be too slow, so we limit to ~12 accepted swap trials with 2500-iteration polishes, keeping eval_time acceptable while giving a real chance of escaping the plateau).
